summary: The main article describes a nickel-catalyzed regioselective addition/cyclization of alkyne-nitriles with arylboronic acids. It includes one table for optimization of reaction conditions, two tables detailing the substrate scope for arylboronic acids and propargyl ethers, and three schemes illustrating the reaction concept, mechanistic studies, and the proposed catalytic cycle.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Metal-catalyzed cascade addition/cyclization reactions.
items.description: Compares known metal-catalyzed syn-addition/cyclization reactions with the current work's unique anti-addition regioselectivity leading to endo-alkenes.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization studies for the formation of 1-naphthylamine 2a
items.description: Lists various catalysts, ligands, bases, and solvents screened to optimize the yield of the cyclization product 2a.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Scope of the reaction with respect to arylboronic acids a
items.description: Displays the chemical structures and yields for 1-naphthylamine products synthesized using different aryl- and heteroarylboronic acids.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Scope of the o -(cyano)phenyl propargyl ethers a
items.description: Shows the scope of the reaction with various substituted o-(cyano)phenyl propargyl ethers and their resulting yields.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Mechanistic studies.
items.description: Illustrates stoichiometric reactions and control experiments used to identify Ni(I) intermediates and rule out allene pathways.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Possible reaction mechanism.
items.description: Proposes a catalytic cycle involving Ni(0), Ni(I), and Ni(II) species, highlighting the anti-carbonickelation step.
